output.editorial_thesis: Southwest's Q2 2025 hedge exit shows why closing contracts and finishing their effect on reported expenses are separate events. The cash received on closure, premium expense recognized that quarter and premium expense deferred in AOCI answer different questions. Reading them on their own clocks avoids treating a closed portfolio as a completed income-statement story, double-counting the proceeds or mistaking an accounting balance for a fresh cash bill.
output.reader_question: How can Southwest have closed its remaining fuel hedges in Q2 2025 while the same filing still described hedge-premium expense flowing into fuel costs through 2027?
output.countercase: Explaining deferred recognition does not establish whether closing the hedges was economically wise. A later expense entry can reflect earlier premiums without proving new contracts, but that accounting distinction also does not prove that fuel-price risk disappeared, that the closure saved money overall or that any later earnings outcome was caused by it. The retained passage cannot settle those questions.
